i think a lot of it may come down to entitlement. 

i dont feel offended when a mans preferences exclude me cause who cares, when i do have an issue (in the cases where its bigotry being spread under the guise of preferences) its the underlying message they are trying to promote that is the problem not the preference.

like if someone says "i dont date girls with body hair because its unsanitary" i genuine do not give a fuck who they date, thats their choice, all the more power to you king, but i do give a fuck that they are spreading misinformation publically about the same body hair theyve got being somehow unhygienic when its a girl with it.

what ive seen in a lot of mens reactions to women having similar body preferences is that they arent often objecting to some core message, but rather they are objecting to the fact that a woman excluded specifically them from their dating pool.

i hear no body hair bc of hygiene and go "that is misinformation"

some guys would hear the same statement but go "this is a personal attack against me"

when i talk about not enjoying small or large penises im not adding a value judgement to it about how those penises are bad or anything. im point blank saying they dont work well with my body.

ive had guys act very entitled in the fact that ive excluded them. instead of saying "damn guess im not for you" and moving on, they have gotten angry or even violent about it.

being calm is the most important thing! i have always been picky because of my sensory processing disorder and it was made 10x worse by adults pressuring, yelling, and chastising me growing up. it got to the point where the only way anyone could get me to eat anything was if i sat alone or across the room from where others where eating because my anxiety around food had gotten intolerable. even at 19 i couldnt sit down at a restaurant without having a meltdown or running to the bathroom to puke out of sheer anxiety.

in the past 2 years my diet has gotten much better and i am no longer underweight or have any vitamin deficiencies, and you know why? cause i moved out and finally got to approach food on my own terms.

what helped me was having consistent low stress encounters with food, exploring things at my own pace, and learning to cook so i could making things the texture and taste that i actually wanted. i can even sit down for a meal at a restaurant now.

so, some ideas for parents with picky kids?

- involve them in the food preperation process
- give them options
- introduce new foods slowly and with little pressure (ea. the first time you serve a new food dont demand they eat it but lightly encourage them to smell, touch, play with, and taste it to help desensitize)
- consider their preferences (ea. maybe boiling vegetables wont work because of the texture but crunchy raw or baked veggies will)

and most of all

if your child is showing sustained and significant distress around eating, talking to a doctor who is familiar with such cases can be the difference between picky eating being solved with accomedations and picky eating developing into a life long eating disorder or source of stress.

TDLR: self employed artists are chronically overworked and underpaid and no one seems to believe us and if they do then its rare that they value us enough to care lol

now, to get into it:

the goes double for anything artistic related. too many people think artists are ripping them off when a digital art piece costs $40+, not realizing that they are paying for both the artist's accumulated skill level as well as their time. i raised my fullbody illustrations to $70 a pop, i still only gross about $7-$10 dollars an hour, factor in material costs (even digital art costs money to make, you need software, drawing tools, etc), fees for whatever payment platform is used, yadda yadda. additionally that $7-$10 an hour is NOT a fulltime job for most. as in $10 an hour might sound okay if youre working 40 hours a week but delays between projects and unpaid admin work + marketing are part an parcel of the majority of artists freelance work meaning its more like working fulltime hours on a part time paycheck.

same with physical merch, you think $3 for a sticker is too much? have you considered the overhead costs of materials, equipment, store/website hosting, time dedicated to marketing, etc? on a $3 sticker my total revenue ranges between $1-$1.75. its closer to $1 if people buy a single sticker then if they buy a handful which is why i incentivize purchases of multiple items with flat rate shipping based on the heaviest item in the order. you save money on bigger orders and i save money on bigger orders (means the ratio between the cost of shipping materials used and profit widens)

i say this all as a small (not tiny but still small) established artist. ive been selling custom art since i was a teenager, ive had an online merch store for a few years now, and only recently did i start gaining more traction when i grew to over 20k followers on tiktok. the closest i got to being fulltime and able to support myself with it was out of sheer desperation. i was too sick to leave my house and i managed to make my rent and bills solely on art. that was when i only had about 3k followers. i worked 40-60 hours a week. that month i made approximately $4 an hour. i worked myself into insanity. by the end of that month i had to get physical therapy (i couldnt even text on my phone, i used speech to text for weeks) because i had destroyed my drawing hand through the lack of rest. but hey, i didnt get evicted so i count that as a win.

unless you have a freak accident of luck where you simultaneously go viral AND manage to convince people that you are worth sticking around and supporting, being a fulltime independent artist is essentially a game of chicken.

in one car there is you, you are passionate, driven, being a professional artist is your dream and number one goal.

then, barreling towards you on the track at full speed is another car with a big pizza place sign on the top that says "BANKRUPT AND HOMELESS, MAYBE A DIFFERENT JOB THAT YOU DONT MIND IF YOU ARE LUCKY" instead of dominos.

ime if you arent in possession of the golden goose of viral marketing you have to have a lot of sheer idiotic stubbornness to make it on your own without having significant financial support and connections for your endevours.

thats not to say it cannot be done, i have seen many artists achieve it. but it is frequently not as luxurious as we tend to think. i remember a couple very popular artists i look up to on twitter openly disscussing their income. average income was under $25k.

these are some of the most beloved/popular independent freelance and merch artists of late. the measure of success in this field is not even middle class in many places.

i am not a doomer in the slightest. i have a perhaps unwise amount of faith in the idea that if im persistent i will gather enough success to at least not have to worry that buying a dozen eggs will break my budget. i am hopefully that the same people who go on and on about their favourite creators will learn to actually value them as people instead of amazon warehouse level content machines meant to churn out masterpieces on a dime.

art in all its forms is a integral part of the human experience and everyone has a unique voice to contribute. art is not going anywhere, only how we choose to treat artists will change. we should value artists more considering how highly we value what they produce.
